s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue with difficulty in mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement leading to difficulty with mastication
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Restriction of mobility requiring diapers
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Managed conservatively with transfusions
Taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements due to deficiencies
Platelet count: 171 × 10^3/μL
Prothrombin time: 11.7 seconds
Activated partial thromboplastin time: 36.0 seconds
Serum zinc: 34.4 μg/dL
Biopsy findings showed subepidermal blister lined by fibrin and chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Direct immunofluorescence test was negative
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the biopsy findings showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining are consistent with amyloidosis, which can cause skin blisters and ulcers, macroglossia, and peripheral neuropathy

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Direct immunofluorescence test was negative, which is not typical for paraneoplastic pemphigus

rejected.label: Zinc deficiency disorder
rejected.why: While the patient has a low serum zinc level, the biopsy findings and other clinical features are more consistent with amyloidosis

rejected.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show linear IgA deposits, which are characteristic of this condition

rejected.label: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of a history of skin fragility or blistering make this diagnosis less likely
